attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own newsletter. The Bloomberg Intelligence estimate that follows it is attributed to someone else and is not part of the claim.

semantics.note: 'Certain to become' is a high-confidence forecast, so it is scored. The four companies are named in the context. The revision correctly dropped the 'to fund AI' purpose, which he did not state. No deadline is given.

contract.note: Reading this as at least one completed bond issuance per company after publication is an ordinary reading. Ruling out loans and equity is fair. The flag that 'repeat' might mean several further visits does not change the result here.

evidence.note: Bloomberg reports Alphabet's completed $25B ten-tranche sale on Aug 6, 2026, after publication. That satisfies one of the four companies only.
El País (Sept 10) reports Amazon launching a sterling bond offering. It shows a launch, not a verified completed issuance. Nothing in the packet covers Meta or Microsoft.

reviews.rationale: Alphabet's return to the bond market after publication is confirmed. Amazon's is only shown as launched, and the packet has no evidence for Meta or Microsoft. No deadline was stated and no event makes issuance impossible, so the claim stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own article.

semantics.note: 'Can or will ever' is a firm, unlimited negative forecast. The $2 trillion threshold is kept. 'Hyperscaler AI spending' fairly stands in for 'any of this' given the context. Whether the $2 trillion is annual or cumulative is not specified.

contract.note: A 'never' claim cannot be confirmed by any finite period of low revenue. It can only be contradicted by a verified crossing of the threshold. The open questions about scope (annual or cumulative, whose revenue counts) are flagged but do not affect the current result.

evidence.note: Reuters reports Anthropic's 2025 revenue of about $4.6B, with 47% sold through cloud marketplaces. It is one company's figure and does not measure industry-wide new revenue.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The packet shows no verified crossing of $2 trillion and no permanent ending of the activity. Current revenue cannot show eventual failure or success, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own article.

semantics.note: The causal chain is kept in his order, including the 'meaningful' qualifier and 'forced to raise more debt'.

contract.note: Reading 'forced' as borrowing that was actually necessary, and 'meaningful' as financially material, is ordinary. The result does depend on those readings, which the speaker did not define.

evidence.note: Micron's own disclosure of record AI-era demand. It fits the demand link but does not measure price pass-through or hyperscaler borrowing.
Secondary report of analyst estimates that memory costs are inflating server prices. These are mostly forecasts, and the report has no link to debt.
Alphabet's own statement attributing Cloud growth to AI demand. It challenges the 'no meaningful improvement' premise, but it does not isolate AI revenue or cash flow.

reviews.rationale: The evidence fits rising memory demand and some cost pressure, but it does not establish price pass-through into server costs, the borrowing being necessary, or that AI's financial contribution was immaterial. Alphabet's own claims of AI-driven growth push the other way but do not settle the matter.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own article.

semantics.note: A vague claim that costs and the required payoff escalate as the buildout continues. 'AI buildout' is a fair reading of 'this' in context.

contract.note: Excluding simple growth in cumulative spending is an interpretation the speaker did not supply. Still, the surrounding text argues that unit costs and debt costs are rising, so the escalation reading is fair. 'Cost' and 'payoff' are undefined, so the reading decides the result.

evidence.note: 2025 Turner & Townsend report: AI data centres are larger and costlier. It shows cost pressure, not escalation caused by continued buildout, and nothing about the required payoff.
August 2026 preprint finding that token prices fell while the price per completed task stopped falling. It measures inference pricing, not construction or investment recovery.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows cost pressure in construction and mixed signals on inference pricing. It has no matched cost series or lifecycle calculation showing that continued buildout raises all-in costs and the payoff required. Not settled.
